If you specifically want a **blue Staffordshire Bull Terrier (Staffy) puppy near Glasgow**, there are several current listings, but I’d treat the adverts as leads rather than endorsements.

### Current places to look

- [royalkennelclub.com](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?ActiveCertifiedBreeder=False&Breeds=Staffordshire+Bull+Terrier&Distance=15&FemaleDogs=False&GeneralRescueClubs=False&HealthTested=False&MaleDogs=False&SearchRescueClubs=False&SortNearest=False&TotalResults=0&utm_source=chatgpt.com) — this is the first place I’d check. You can filter for Staffordshire Bull Terriers, location and health-tested parents. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?ActiveCertifiedBreeder=False&Breeds=Staffordshire+Bull+Terrier&Distance=15&FemaleDogs=False&GeneralRescueClubs=False&HealthTested=False&MaleDogs=False&SearchRescueClubs=False&SortNearest=False&TotalResults=0&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [pets4homes.co.uk](https://www.pets4homes.co.uk/sale/puppies/staffordshire-bull-terrier/united-kingdom/scotland/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) — currently shows several blue Staffy litters around Scotland, including listings in Glasgow, Largs and Kilmarnock. [Pets4Homes](https://www.pets4homes.co.uk/sale/puppies/staffordshire-bull-terrier/united-kingdom/scotland/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [pets4homes.co.uk](https://www.pets4homes.co.uk/classifieds/cfbu1g7mi-beautiful-pure-english-blue-staffys-pups-for-sale-glasgow/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) — one Glasgow litter is advertised at £900, with the seller stating that both parents are health-tested and that the pups will be microchipped, vaccinated and vet-checked. Verify all of this independently before paying anything. [Pets4Homes](https://www.pets4homes.co.uk/classifieds/cfbu1g7mi-beautiful-pure-english-blue-staffys-pups-for-sale-glasgow/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [pets4homes.co.uk](https://www.pets4homes.co.uk/classifieds/w-tn62x4-blue-staffordshire-bull-terrier-puppies-glasgow/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) — a separate litter is currently advertised as KC registered, with health-tested parents, at £2,500. Again, check the documentation rather than relying on the advert. [Pets4Homes](https://www.pets4homes.co.uk/classifieds/w-tn62x4-blue-staffordshire-bull-terrier-puppies-glasgow/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

I **wouldn't choose purely on colour**. Blue is actually an accepted Staffordshire Bull Terrier colour under the Royal Kennel Club breed standard, despite sometimes being marketed as a "rare" colour. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/breeds-a-to-z/breeds/terrier/staffordshire-bull-terrier/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) [SC Staffordshire Bull Terrier Society](https://www.scsbts.com/sbt-welfare-and-rescue/buying-a-puppy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) 

### What to ask the breeder

Before putting down a deposit, ask:

1. **Can I see the puppy with its mother and the rest of the litter at your home?**
 You should see the mother interacting normally with her puppies. Be very cautious if you're offered a meeting somewhere else or the mother is mysteriously unavailable.
2. **What health tests have both parents had, and can I see the certificates?**
 Don't settle for "they're health tested." Ask exactly **which tests**, the results and the dates. The Royal Kennel Club specifically recommends checking that parents have been health tested according to the breed-specific advice. [Royal Kennel Club](https://www.royalkennelclub.com/search/find-a-puppy/?ActiveCertifiedBreeder=False&Breeds=Staffordshire+Bull+Terrier&Distance=15&FemaleDogs=False&GeneralRescueClubs=False&HealthTested=False&MaleDogs=False&SearchRescueClubs=False&SortNearest=False&TotalResults=0&utm_source=chatgpt.com)
3. **Can I see the parents' KC registration details and pedigrees?**
 KC registration establishes pedigree; it isn't, by itself, proof that the parents are free from every inherited condition.
4. **What is the puppy's health record?**
 Ask for the vet examination, microchip details, vaccination/worming history and any relevant health paperwork.
5. **How have the puppies been socialised?**
 Ask whether they've experienced children, household noises, visitors, handling, different surfaces, crates and car journeys. Early socialisation is particularly important with Staffies. [PDSA](https://www.pdsa.org.uk/pet-help-and-advice/looking-after-your-pet/puppies-dogs/medium-dogs/staffordshire-bull-terrier?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
6. **How many litters does the mother have, and how old is she?**
 Ask how many times she's been bred and when she last had puppies.
7. **Can I meet the father?**
 Ideally see him too. If he isn't on the premises, ask for his registered name, health results and pedigree.
8. **What happens if I develop a problem with the puppy?**
 A responsible breeder should have a contract and be willing to take the dog back or help rehome it rather than simply disappearing after the sale.

### Red flags 🚩

I'd walk away if the breeder:

- Wants a deposit before allowing you to visit.
- Won't let you see the mother.
- Has multiple breeds/litters constantly available.
- Pressures you with "someone else is coming to buy him today."
- Can't produce health-test certificates.
- Wants to meet in a car park or other neutral location.
- Advertises unusual colours such as **merle** as desirable or rare; merle isn't a recognised Staffordshire Bull Terrier colour. [SC Staffordshire Bull Terrier Society](https://www.scsbts.com/sbt-welfare-and-rescue/buying-a-puppy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- Focuses heavily on phrases like "XL," "micro," "rare blue," "huge head" or "champion bloodline" while providing little health information.

One other point: **don't assume a higher price means a better-bred or healthier puppy**. Current Glasgow adverts range considerably in price, so I'd make the documented health testing, breeding practices and puppy's upbringing the important comparison.

If you tell me **how far you're willing to travel from Glasgow (e.g. 30, 60 or 100 miles) and whether you want a male or female**, I can narrow down the current listings and help you make a shortlist of breeders to contact.
